cases.description: A UTF-8 byte order mark at byte 0 of a JSON record is skipped (§5.1), as RFC 8259 lets a parser do.
A byte order mark at byte 0 of a YAML record is skipped (§5.1).
Only the byte order mark at byte 0 is one; a second U+FEFF is an ordinary character, which JSON does not allow outside a string, so the record is a syntax error.
A raw U+FEFF inside a JSON string is an ordinary character and stays in the value (§5.1).
A raw U+FEFF inside a quoted YAML scalar, where YAML allows it, is an ordinary character and stays (§5.1).
YAML does not allow U+FEFF in a plain scalar (nb-char excludes it), so the record is a syntax error, although the yaml package accepts it (§5.1, decision J4).

A second U+FEFF after the byte order mark of a YAML file is one YAML would read as a byte order mark other than at byte 0, so it is a syntax error, although the yaml package strips it (§5.1, decision J4).
YAML does not allow U+FEFF in a block scalar, so the record is a syntax error, although the yaml package accepts it (§5.1, decision J4).
YAML does not allow U+FEFF in a comment either, so the record is a syntax error, although the yaml package accepts it (§5.1, decision J4).
A U+FEFF at the start of a line after a comment line is a syntax error, although the yaml package strips it there as a byte order mark (§5.1, decision J4).
